Date: 2026-12-15 / Time: 14:00 UTC / Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Kim (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood CSM); Sofia Martinez (Archway Head of Partnerships), Daniel Wu (Archway Partner Sales), Priya Nair (Archway Channel Ops)

summary: Quarter-end co-sell pipeline review with Archway Partners focusing on three priority joint deals (RetailCo pilot, HealthX procurement, FinServe renewal). Discussed roles, pricing alignment, technical asks for pilots (VPC/private deployment for HealthX, latency SLOs for RetailCo), and next steps including pilot kickoff and joint account mapping. Agreed to run cost/latency scenarios and share partner playbook.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Okay good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have an hour scheduled, we'll run through the three priority deals and the co-sell motions.
[00:08] Sofia Martinez: Hi all, thanks. Quick heads-up I'm on a slightly shaky connection - if I drop just flag me.
[00:14] Jordan Kim: no worries, we can repeat stuff. so first up RetailCo, Maya do you want to kick off the commercial ask?
[00:20] Maya Patel: Sure. RetailCo is asking for a 90 day pilot, 50k committed spend, they want dedicated capacity or at least a reserved pool during peak hours. Archway will own the account exec motion, we'll be co-selling.
[00:34] Daniel Wu: Yep, and from Archway side we will handle introductions to the buyer and the SOW. they want a predictable latency under 300ms for 512-token prompts - that's their soft SLO.
[00:46] Jordan Kim: right. from a technical lens we recommended Redwood Dedicated for throughput, but we can also do a mixed routing: hosted for non-critical traffic and dedicated during peak windows. That reduces cost.
[01:02] Priya Nair: question, is there a difference in data residency or encryption between hosted and dedicated? we have a security checklist for RetailCo.
[01:10] Maya Patel: good q - Dedicated gives isolated GPU pools and the data plane stays within their cloud region. We can also enable customer-managed KMS. For stricter regs we'd suggest Redwood Private.
[01:24] Sofia Martinez: RetailCo likely won't need private, but HealthX does - they demanded on-prem or VPC with HSM.
[01:31] Jordan Kim: HealthX is the tricky one. If they require HSM + air-gapped, we'll need the Private deployment; that'll add lead time. Also we should discuss certs - SOC 2, ISO 27001 are in place but HealthX asked for SOC2 Type II and audit logs retention to 2 years.
[01:47] Maya Patel: yeah we're SOC 2 Type II compliant and have audit logs; I can share the security pack after this call (link: https://redwood.example/sec-pack).
[01:56] Daniel Wu: can you also include SSO/SAML and RBAC notes - HealthX will check integration with Okta.
[02:03] Jordan Kim: We'll include the SSO doc; technical note - Private supports existing IdP flows and we can sync to customer directory.
[02:12] Sofia Martinez: Great. moving to pricing, Archway generally asks for 10-15% partner margin on list pricing. Are you able to support partner tiers for pilots?
[02:22] Maya Patel: For pilots we can offer a promotional tier - typically 12% partner cut on committed pilot spend. For larger enterprise renewals we can do rebate-style credits. I'll put these in the playbook.
[02:34] Daniel Wu: sounds good. On the RetailCo pilot, Archway would like to own the POC but Redwood to provide SE time for architecture and a short benchmarking report.
[02:44] Jordan Kim: we can allocate up to 8 hours of SE assistance during pilot; we'll run a baseline latency/cost sweep using their prompt set. Can you share the prompt examples?
[02:54] Sofia Martinez: yes will share prompt set and a sample dataset - sending after meeting.
[03:00] Maya Patel: Perfect. Next, FinServe renewal - this one's mid-deal, 200k ARR target, client is sensitive to compliance and wants detailed SLA.
[03:12] Daniel Wu: FinServe is leaning toward HelixTech currently because Helix offered a managed private bundle. we need a clear differentiator.
[03:21] Jordan Kim: Differentiators: transparent token-level cost, built-in KV cache to accelerate repeated prompts, and our rolling rollouts with automatic fallback. For FinServe, we should propose a dedicated with optional private snapshot for audits.
[03:35] Priya Nair: any performance numbers we can share now? average p50/p95?
[03:40] Jordan Kim: p50 for 256 tokens is ~70ms on our dx-optimized path, p95 about 230ms, that's on dedicated A100-ish class; I'll confirm exact numbers for the FinServe workload once we have sequence length distribution.
[03:53] Maya Patel: Jordan will produce a latency/cost spreadsheet for FinServe and RetailCo. Jordan, can you include quantized vs FP16 options?
[04:02] Jordan Kim: yes, I'll include 4-bit quantization profiles, impact on latency and slight quality delta notes.
[04:09] Sofia Martinez: on the partner motion, we need a co-sell playbook that shows lead routing, commission splits, and intro templates.
[04:16] Maya Patel: Agreed - I'm drafting a partner playbook. I'll add lead routing flows (partner-first, AE-assist), sample intro email and template SOW.
[04:26] Daniel Wu: also, for the RetailCo vendor evaluation they asked for benchmark artifacts - can Redwood provide a short benchmark report and a recording of a model run?
[04:35] Jordan Kim: yes we'll run a benchmark with their prompt set, capture token-level cost, latency, and a short demo clip. Expect the spreadsheet link in 3 business days.
[04:45] Priya Nair: timeline question: RetailCo pilot wants kickoff week of Jan 5th - are we aligned?
[04:52] Maya Patel: we can probably hit that if contracts signed by end of year. Archway to get buyer intro ASAP.
[04:58] Sofia Martinez: we'll aim to get internal approvals and send intros this week.
[05:03] Jordan Kim: quick technical note: RetailCo uses multi-region traffic spikes; we'd recommend setting auto-scaling burst capacity + prefix caching to reduce cold-start KV hits. Also set a routing policy for EU region.
[05:18] Daniel Wu: on discounts - if RetailCo commits to 3 months after pilot, can partner margins be bumped?
[05:24] Maya Patel: Yes, if they commit to a 9-month roll we'll offer up to 18% partner margin or equivalent credits. I'll add thresholds to the playbook.
[05:34] Sofia Martinez: HealthX pilot - they want an on-site demo and a short security whiteboard session. who owns the whiteboard?
[05:41] Maya Patel: Jordan and our security PM can run the whiteboard. Jordan will coordinate the technical deep dive and I will coordinate commercial.
[05:48] Jordan Kim: note - HealthX's engineering team is heavy on latency and traceability; we should propose Redwood Console access for their SREs. It gives token-level traces, error analysis.
[05:58] Priya Nair: will they get full Console or read-only? they'll ask for least privilege.
[06:03] Jordan Kim: we can grant read-only dashboards and create RBAC roles.
[06:08] Maya Patel: recap - action items: playbook, account list, latency/cost sheet, SE hours for pilot, and security pack.
[06:15] Sofia Martinez: correct. any blockers from Archway side? the only blocker is we need transparent pricing to baseline our partner margin calculations.
[06:24] Maya Patel: I'll send a partner pricing tiers doc today.
[06:28] Daniel Wu: one more thing - competitor mention: NimbusAI approached FinServe with managed infra, how should we position?
[06:36] Maya Patel: emphasize our unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private and cost controls; highlight rollout safety and observability. Also mention our Optimize recommendations for batching/caching.
[06:48] Jordan Kim: quick heads-up - for HealthX Private deployment, lead time is ~8 weeks for on-prem validation plus provisioning; plan accordingly.
[06:57] Sofia Martinez: noted.
[07:00] Maya Patel: okay last thing: who will be point for the RetailCo intro? Sofia?
[07:04] Sofia Martinez: yes I'll send the intro and include Maya and Jordan.
[07:09] Liam O'Connor: I'll open a joint Salesforce opportunity and share the link after the call (will add CRMD-48721).
[07:16] Maya Patel: perfect. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the playbook and the latency/cost spreadsheet.
[07:22] Daniel Wu: thanks all.
[07:24] Priya Nair: thanks.
[07:25] Sofia Martinez: bye
[07:26] [Meeting ends]
